Author: Arzhael
Name: AutoStanceXIV
Description:
Keeps your tank stance in the state you choose (on or off) on every tank: Paladin/Gladiator, Warrior/Marauder, Dark Knight and Gunbreaker.
Apply it always, or only at specific moments: zone change, resurrection, job change, countdown, pull (bosses only), duty recommence after a wipe.
Classic mode uses the same settings everywhere; advanced mode has separate settings for the open world, dungeons, trials, raids and alliance raids.
Optional: automatic level sync when you enter a FATE.
Available in English and French. Command: /autostance
Punchline: Automatically turns your tank stance on or off.

Author: Arzhael
Name: FlashColor
Description:
Adjust exposure, contrast, saturation, vibrance and white balance inside the game's own tone mapping, before the image is cut to what the screen can show. Bright effects such as flames keep their gradient and their color instead of turning into flat white or yellow patches, textures keep their details, and the game's interface is never touched.
Also: shadows, midtones and lights, per-color settings, sharpness and clarity, presets (and your own), the game's GPose filters everywhere, and a cutscene-like white flash.
Available in English and French. Command: /flashcolor
Punchline: Contrast and color balance for the game's image, without clipping flames and bright effects.

Author: Arzhael
Name: GposeFilterXIV
Description:
Pick a filter from the game's GPose list and an intensity (0-100 %, like the GPose slider): GposeFilterXIV keeps it on everywhere, outside of GPose.
The game draws the filter itself, exactly as in GPose: no shader, no hook for the filter. The window is made of the game's own interface elements. Cutscenes and GPose filters take over while they need it, then yours comes back. Turning it off or unloading the plugin gives back the area's own filter.
Available in English and French. Command: /gposefilter
Punchline: Keeps one of the game's GPose color filters on outside of GPose.

Author: Arzhael
Name: LootFinderXIV
Punchline: The loot sheet of every duty: rare rewards, tomestones and coffers.
Description: Shows a database-style loot sheet for each duty: rare rewards (minions, mounts, orchestrion rolls) obtained or not, tomestones and gil per boss, and the content of every coffer with what you already own. Opens next to the Duty Finder or from the server info bar. Interface in English and French.
Changelog: 1.3.0: search bar in the duty list, alliance raids in their own group, language setting, long names cut with an ellipsis.

Author: Arzhael
Name: OffStreamXIV
Description:
Choose what your stream sees: hide a whole plugin, or only its main window, its settings or some of its windows, from OBS and other capture software (game, window and display capture). They stay visible on your screen. Texts that plugins add inside game windows (for example Character Panel Refined in the Character window) can be hidden too.
Requires Dalamud's "Enable multi-monitor windows" setting, the game in windowed or borderless window mode, and more than one monitor.
Available in English and French. Command: /offstream
Punchline: Hide plugin windows from your stream (OBS and other capture software) while you keep seeing them.

Author: Arzhael
Name: OutfitPackerXIV
Description:
When you open the Glamour Dresser, OutfitPackerXIV lists the pieces of gear that belong to the same outfit: complete outfits ready to be stored, incomplete ones with their missing pieces, outfits already stored that a loose piece can join, and duplicates. For each one, it shows how many dresser slots you would free.
The Pack button stores an outfit for you: it takes its pieces out of the dresser one at a time, then stores them as an outfit (the game uses up to one Glamour Prism per piece and removes dyes: undyed copies come first, and it asks before taking a piece that is only there dyed).
The Inventory tab finds outfit pieces in your bags and armory chest and stores them directly, leaving aside pieces with materia, a glamour, or used by a gear set.
The Remove button takes extra copies out of the dresser into your inventory, keeping one for each outfit that still needs the piece. It never throws anything away.
Available in English and French. Command: /outfitpacker
Punchline: Finds the outfits you can store in the Glamour Dresser and packs them for you to free up its slots.

Author: Arzhael
Name: RefBoardXIV
Description:
A reference board in a game window: drag images from the Windows explorer or paste them, zoom with the mouse wheel, move, resize and crop them. Several boards, which you can share with other players as a single file, a locked mode where only the images stay and clicks go to the game, customizable keyboard shortcuts, and automatic hiding in cutscenes, gpose, combat or loading screens.
Available in English and French. Command: /refboard
Punchline: A reference board inside the game: drop images, zoom, move them around.

Author: Arzhael
Name: Simple HUD
Description:
Adds "Flying Text" frames to the HUD layout editor: drag them to choose where the text about your character appears (healing received, status effects and damage taken), and set its size or hide it.
In the same editor, shows where each HUD element is and lets you set the selected one to the pixel.
Available in English and French. Command: /simplehud
Punchline: Simple, pixel-precise tweaks to your HUD and flying text, right from the HUD layout editor.
